mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate sales (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between HOUST declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month for 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to increased liquidity and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances following a FEDFUNDS decrease, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling retail sales (RSAFS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls and UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
